context: camera + battery life for daily driver
body: The 2026 refresh focuses on the camera (improved low-light + variable aperture) and battery (claimed 25% longer, measured 18% in daily mixed use). Build quality is as expected. The downside is price — ¥180,000+ out of pocket. If you keep phones for 4+ years, it works out. For 2-year cycles, consider the base iPhone 17 instead.

context: replacing XM5 after 2 years of commute use
body: Noise canceling is noticeably better than XM5 on planes and trains. Call quality improved too — the beam-forming mics actually filter wind now. 30-hour battery holds up. Negative: the carrying case got bigger. Price-wise, wait for a Prime Day/BF discount to get ~¥35,000 instead of ¥50,000 MSRP.

item.name: ユニクロ エアリズム T

body: Still the baseline. ¥1,000, wicks sweat, dries fast on an interior rack overnight. Buy 5, rotate. The 2026 version has slightly reinforced neck seams — the one weak point of previous years. No reason to pay more unless you need merino wool for odor control.

item.name: ワークマン クライミングパンツ

body: The classic reason people joke about Workman replacing Patagonia. Fit is a bit narrow around the thigh if you have cycling-trained legs. Water resistance is 'light drizzle' only. For ¥2,000, it's unbeatable value — I use mine for both weekend climbing and WFH days.

The MALM has been a dorm/apartment default for 25 years because it's cheap and tidy. But: (1) assembly takes 90-120 minutes for first-timers. (2) must anchor to wall per Ikea's recall warning (don't skip this). (3) drawer slides are plastic, not metal — long-term they get sticky. For ¥25,000 you can do better now with Nitori's equivalent.

item.name: ニトリ Nクール 枕

context: summer sleep in a non-aircon room
body: The cool-touch fabric feels genuinely cool for the first 30 seconds. After that your body heat warms it like any other pillow. For ¥1,500 it's a cheap morale boost in August. For actual summer cooling, a USB-powered neck fan does more. Pillow shape (height) is average — not for stomach sleepers.

item.name: ラーメン二郎 三田本店
item.description: The flagship of the Jiro ramen chain.

body: The original Jiro. 60-minute line at 12:00. Portion is 1,400kcal+ even on 'small'. Order with mashi mashi ninnikuyasai if you're a first-timer and want to appear knowledgeable. One bowl ¥950. Weak point: you cannot order modifications, you cannot leave soup. Don't bring a date.

¥400, 10 minutes door-to-door. Rice-to-beef ratio is stingy vs Yoshinoya but the beni-shouga is free and unlimited. 24/7 locations near every station. The paid upgrade to tokumori is only ¥180 and worth it. For comparison with Yoshinoya: Sukiya is slightly sweeter sauce, slightly worse beef quality — depends on taste.

item.name: APAホテル 新宿御苑前

context: overnight stay after a late Tokyo meeting
body: ¥9,000-13,000/night. Rooms are tiny (12-15㎡) but functional. Bed is their trademark firm style — some love it, some hate it. Breakfast is bland. Location vs Shinjuku station is a 7-min walk. The main criticism: visible political materials in the lobby make it awkward for international guests. If that bothers you, Toyoko Inn or Mitsui Garden is a cleaner choice at similar price.

¥5,000-9,000 one-way if booked 2+ weeks ahead. ANA/JAL is 3-4x. Seats are tight; add Simple Peach fare and you get checked baggage. On-time performance has improved — 85% within 15 minutes based on 6 round trips in 2026. Avoid during obon/GW weeks; fare matches JAL and bags cost extra. For solo weekend trips, no reason to pay full-service price.

¥1,280/mo. The ad removal alone is worth it if you watch more than 1h/day. YT Music is weaker than Spotify's recommendation but matches on catalog. Family plan ¥2,280 for up to 5 people (members do NOT need to live at same address — enforced loosely in Japan). Cancel and resubscribe tactic lets you grab new-user discounts twice a year.

The streak mechanic is extremely effective at building a daily habit. BUT: the English course for JP speakers is thin above B1 level. Grammar explanations are weak compared to competitors (Rosetta Stone is still better here). After 6 months, I switched to Anki + a tutor. Great starter / habit-builder, bad as sole method. Free tier is noisy with ads; Super Duolingo is ¥1,000/mo.

Zero commission on JP stocks (post-2024). US stocks are 0.495%. UI is dated but functional. NISA setup is 2 weeks from signup to live. Better than Rakuten Shoken for US stock access; comparable to Monex. The weak point: customer support is email-only and 2-3 day turnaround. For a passive index investor it doesn't matter.

1% back as Rakuten points on everything. If you shop on Rakuten Market even occasionally, points pile up fast (SPU multipliers). Annual fee ¥0 for life. Weak points: non-visa foreign transactions have a 2.2% FX markup, and the app is spammy with promotions. For international travel, pair with a Sony Bank wallet card.

¥3,278/mo for 24h access. Equipment is minimal (treadmill + basic machines, no squat rack). Target audience is beginners — serious lifters will be bored in a week. Locations are everywhere now. The one thing nobody mentions: there's no shower. If you lift hard, this doesn't work for a commute-to-office pattern. For 20-min cardio or office exercises, it's cheap enough.

The thinner body and brighter display are the main upgrades. Battery is finally a real 2 days on normal use (was 16 hours in series 7). FDA-approved sleep apnea detection is new and surprisingly accurate. Price ¥65,000. The one gripe: if you have an iPhone, it's wonderful; if you ever consider switching to Android, you're locked in.

28 km/L realized fuel economy in city driving. Interior is still a bit plasticky vs Honda Fit, but mechanically rock solid. Resale value is high — plan on recouping ~60% at 5 years. The CVT whine is noticeable above 80 km/h. For a daily commuter, nothing beats it on operating cost.

item.name: ロイヤルカナン インドア (キャット)
item.description: Dry cat food for indoor-only cats.

context: feeding two adult indoor cats for 4 years
body: Vet-recommended, consistent product. Our cats' coat improved vs the cheaper supermarket brands. The 'indoor' formula reduces stool odor noticeably. Price is ¥4,500 for 4kg which lasts two cats about 5 weeks. Weak point: palatability drops after bag is open for ~3 weeks (switch to smaller bags if you have 1 cat).

item.name: ゼルダの伝説 ティアーズオブザキングダム

body: Builds on BOTW's open world with Ultrahand (combine any two objects) and the sky/underground layers. 150 hours to feel 'done'. Framerate dips below 30 in dense areas but it's playable. Nothing else on Switch comes close. Only reservation: if you've played BOTW it feels iterative at times. New players should start here.

OLED screen is a legitimate upgrade over LCD. Battery is 60-80% better. Steam compatibility is great; non-Steam launchers (EA/Ubisoft) take work. Weight is 640g — tiring for 2h+ sessions in bed. For Japan: no local warranty, imports via Komodo at ~¥85,000. If you own a gaming PC, this complements it; if you don't, it IS your gaming PC.

item.name: SKII フェイシャルトリートメントエッセンス

body: The signature product. Pitera is a real yeast ferment with evidence behind it, but you're paying ¥18,000 for 160ml. Noticeable skin texture improvement at 2 months. If you can afford it indefinitely, works. If you can't, Minon's amino acid lotion at 1/10 the price gives 60% of the benefit. Buy at duty-free (Narita/Haneda) for ~25% off.

¥500 for 169g, lasts a year. Formula is basically mineral oil + glycerin. Thick enough to seal moisture, not fragranced like competitors. Famous Reddit lifehack 'blue can is basically La Mer' is partially true — the ingredient overlap is 60%+. For Japan winter, this is the baseline. Dries down greasy; apply at night.
